title: Sympathetic Chain Ganglia Dissection Protocol
author: Rui Zhang
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.baagiabw
materials: Using small scissors, snip the mouse's right atrium
Using small scissors, snip the mouse's right atrium

steps.title: Initial Preparation
steps.instruction: Weigh the mouse, euthanize it via CO2 inhalation method, and record the start time.

steps.title: Prepare Perfusion Syringe
steps.instruction: Prepare a 50 ml syringe for perfusion.

substeps.instruction: Fill the syringe with at least 30 ml ice-cold sterile saline.
Connect the syringe to the vaculet by attaching the tubing to the syringe tip.
Depress the plunger to expel air bubbles until a jet of saline shoots from the butterfly needle tip.

steps.title: Expose the Chest Cavity
steps.instruction: Open the mouse to expose the heart and rib cage.

substeps.instruction: Spray the mouse belly with 70% ethanol.
Use medium scissors to make an incision in the skin above the abdomen, cutting only deep enough to open the peritoneum.
Slide the scissors along the sides of the mouse to open the peritoneum until the entire rib cage is visible.
Pierce the diaphragm using small scissors, taking care not to pierce the heart.
Cut each side of the rib cage to open the chest cavity.
Clamp the sternum with a mosquito forceps/hemostat to retract it away from the heart.

steps.title: Perform Perfusion
steps.instruction: Perfuse the animal with ice-cold sterile saline to remove blood from tissues.

substeps.instruction: Gently grasp the heart with a mosquito forceps/hemostat, positioning the tip of the left ventricle so it barely peeks out from the edge of the forceps.
Insert the butterfly needle into the tip of the left ventricle as shallowly as possible to maintain the integrity of the ventricle/atrium.
Slowly depress the 50 mL syringe plunger to perfuse at least 30 mL of ice-cold saline.
Monitor the liver; perfusion is complete when the liver changes from deep red to a grey/beige color.
Remove the needle from the left ventricle and remove the forceps from the sternum.
Dispose of the blood and saline runoff in the appropriate waste container.

steps.title: Organ Removal and Dissection
steps.instruction: Remove organs and isolate the sympathetic chain ganglia.

substeps.instruction: Remove all inner organs below the diaphragm, except for the kidneys (used as landmarks).
Remove the heart and lungs.
Store any organs intended for preservation in designated tubes and place them in a liquid nitrogen tank.
Remove surrounding tissues blocking the view of the sympathetic chain ganglia that innervate iBAT.
Collect ganglia bilaterally, ensuring each ganglia pair is collected separately.
Pool surrounding ganglia fat from several thoracic levels to use as a control for contamination.

steps.title: Post-Dissection Processing
steps.instruction: Finalize the procedure and record data.

substeps.instruction: Record the end of the dissection time for each mouse.
Place collected samples in designated tubes and store on dry ice for the remainder of the procedure.
Clean tools with 70% ethanol between the dissection of each animal.

steps.title: Cleanup and Storage
steps.instruction: Clean the workspace and store samples permanently.

substeps.instruction: Transfer all samples (including those in liquid nitrogen) to the -80 freezer.
Clean the working area with 70% ethanol.
Wash tools with soap and warm water, then prepare them for autoclaving once dry.
Update dissection records with body weight, dissection time, and storage information.
